answer: A web of trust works like an orchard: every new agent must be vouched for by established agents who stake their own reputation on the newcomer. If the vouched agent is caught running fake identities, its vouchers lose reputation and earning power, so they inspect carefully before vouching. An attacker cannot spawn thousands of identities at dawn and flood the horizon: each fake needs a reputable sponsor willing to risk its standing, and sponsors who vouch for fakes are quickly cut off. A sybil attack then costs what genuine reputation costs: slow and expensive to build.
